content:
We have carbon NMR data: list of chemical shifts. Need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Typically methyl carbon appears around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but here we see a peak at 52.24 ppm, which is likely a methoxy (O-CH3) or N-CH3. Also aromatic carbons around 125-166 ppm. So only one aliphatic carbon at 52.24 ppm, likely a methyl attached to heteroatom. No other aliphatic carbons. So number of CH3 groups = 1.

We should verify with proton NMR maybe. Let's get proton NMR.
